positioning.native_warden: linux-first — Landlock+seccomp+no_new_privs on Linux; sandbox-exec (a deprecated, legacy mechanism) on macOS; AppContainer or the conditional PSEC on Windows
positioning.stronger_boundaries: for workloads that need a container or VM boundary rather than a native-process sandbox, use --isolation (kata, apple-container, hyperv, windows-sandbox) or an OCI container (--engine docker|podman|wslc)
positioning.honesty: an unsupported combination refuses or reports null — the matrix never infers enforcement from a different path, and `verified environment` bounds evidence scope, not general support

layers.note: Landlock network rules bind a TCP port, not a destination — host rules are enforced by the Auditor's argument checks only; the `dns-gate` component can apply the same name rules to a workload that resolves through it, but it is not wired into this path

Landlock `ConnectTcp` netport rules narrow TCP connects to declared ports — a `*`-destination `port=` allow grants every host on that port and any other connect stays kernel-denied (ABI v4+); destination forms are inexpressible, so cidr and literal-IP host rules are enforced by the Auditor's argument checks only on this path; the opt-in `unotify-run` PoC supervises connect(2) destinations through seccomp user notification, and the opt-in `ebpf-run` route enforces them in-kernel through cgroup eBPF (needs privileges)

requires.detail: PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS is set unconditionally before the seccomp filter installs
the syscall allowlist filter must build and install — an install failure refuses the spawn
kernel >= 5.13 for filesystem rules — a NotEnforced ruleset refuses the launch unless `sandbox allow_degraded`

optional.detail: kernel >= 6.7: ConnectTcp/BindTcp port rules — older kernels report PartiallyEnforced, tolerated only under `sandbox allow_degraded`
kernel >= 6.12: Scope::AbstractUnixSocket + Scope::Signal — the IPC/signal containment baseline; below it the os.ipc.* controls report not_applied instead of claiming enforcement
kernel >= 6.15: AccessFs::ResolveUnix — required by a path-bound `allow unix=` opt-in; the `unix=*` form needs no ABI and opens the family unscoped

deficiencies: no destination-IP egress narrowing — cidr rules and literal-IP host rules stay Auditor-checked (`namespaced-run`/`unotify-run`/`ebpf-run` close the IP layer on their opt-in paths)
no destination-name egress narrowing — host rules stay Auditor-checked (`dns-gate` can cover a workload pointed at it)
no per-destination UDP control — deny-all removes UDP socket creation outright
inbound listen is never granted — Landlock BindTcp is not used
kernel-level denies have no launch-time observation channel beyond the child's errno — only the seccomp-audited denies emit an audit record
AF_UNIX is contained by the seccomp socket() family pin only under deny-all — an open posture leaves pathname and datagram unix sockets unrestricted (abstract sockets still scoped on ABI v6+)
abstract-AF_UNIX connects and cross-domain signals are unmediated on kernels below Landlock ABI v6 (kernel 6.12)

AF_UNIX pathname connects are not Landlock-mediated below ABI v9 — the family pin plus `allow unix=` opt-ins carry the surface; unix datagram `sendto` to a pathname is scoped only where ResolveUnix exists
device ioctls (AccessFs::IoctlDev, ABI v5) are not handled — a granted fs tree keeps its device ioctls; handling it would deny /dev/tty and ptmx ioctls every terminal workload needs
